# Toggle

One control that stays pressed: bookmark, pin, mute, unread only. The single-item sibling of Toggle Group, sharing its paint and its heights, with a pressed glyph that fills in instead of blinking.

```tsx
<Toggle defaultPressed>
  <EnvelopeSimple weight="bold" /> Unread only
</Toggle>
<Toggle variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Bookmark" defaultPressed>
  <ToggleIcon off={<BookmarkSimple weight="bold" />} on={<BookmarkSimple weight="fill" />} />
</Toggle>
<Toggle variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Pin">
  <ToggleIcon off={<PushPin weight="bold" />} on={<PushPin weight="fill" />} />
</Toggle>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli@latest init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli@latest add toggle
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/toggle/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import { Toggle } from "@/components/ui/toggle"

export function Example() {
  return <Toggle aria-label="Show grid">Show grid</Toggle>
}
```

## Variants

`outline` (the default) is the Toggle Group pill: a framed control whose pressed state is the brand border and a soft halo, with no fill. `ghost` is bare at rest and takes the accent chip once pressed, the Toolbar's pressed look, for icon toggles in a row of other controls. Each is shown off, then on.

```tsx
<Toggle><GridFour weight="bold" /> Show grid</Toggle>
<Toggle defaultPressed><GridFour weight="bold" /> Show grid</Toggle>

<Toggle variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Italic"><TextItalic weight="bold" /></Toggle>
<Toggle variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Bold" defaultPressed><TextB weight="bold" /></Toggle>
```

## Sizes

The Toggle Group scale: `sm` is 32px and `md` (the default) is 40px, so a lone toggle lines up with a group beside it. `iconOnly` squares the control around one glyph and steps the glyph up to 20px at `md`. The 32px control grows its target to 40px (44px on touch) without growing the visual.

```tsx
<Toggle size="sm" defaultPressed><PushPin weight="bold" /> Pin</Toggle>
<Toggle size="sm" iconOnly aria-label="Pin" defaultPressed><PushPin weight="bold" /></Toggle>
<Toggle size="md" defaultPressed><PushPin weight="bold" /> Pin</Toggle>
<Toggle size="md" iconOnly aria-label="Pin" defaultPressed><PushPin weight="bold" /></Toggle>
```

## Pressed glyph

`ToggleIcon` holds two glyphs in one cell and cross-fades them on the toggle's state: the outgoing one shrinks to a quarter, fades and blurs as the incoming one resolves, on a CSS transition, so pressing twice quickly reverses mid-way instead of restarting. Pass the pressed glyph in its `fill` weight, which is how the system marks a selected state, or a different glyph when on means something else (a slashed microphone). Press them.

```tsx
<Toggle variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Bookmark" defaultPressed>
  <ToggleIcon off={<BookmarkSimple weight="bold" />} on={<BookmarkSimple weight="fill" />} />
</Toggle>
<Toggle variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Like">
  <ToggleIcon off={<Heart weight="bold" />} on={<Heart weight="fill" className="text-destructive" />} />
</Toggle>
<Toggle variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Star">
  <ToggleIcon off={<Star weight="bold" />} on={<Star weight="fill" className="text-warning" />} />
</Toggle>
<Toggle variant="ghost" iconOnly aria-label="Mute">
  <ToggleIcon off={<Microphone weight="bold" />} on={<MicrophoneSlash weight="bold" />} />
</Toggle>
```

## With a tooltip

An icon-only toggle is named by its `aria-label`: the glyph is not a name. Show that name to sighted users with a `Tooltip`, and wrap the row in a `TooltipGroup` so the bubble glides from one toggle to the next.

```tsx
<TooltipGroup>
  <Tooltip content={<>Bold <Kbd size="sm">⌘B</Kbd></>}>
    <Toggle variant="ghost" size="sm" iconOnly aria-label="Bold" defaultPressed>
      <TextB weight="bold" />
    </Toggle>
  </Tooltip>
  <Tooltip content={<>Italic <Kbd size="sm">⌘I</Kbd></>}>
    <Toggle variant="ghost" size="sm" iconOnly aria-label="Italic">
      <TextItalic weight="bold" />
    </Toggle>
  </Tooltip>
</TooltipGroup>
```

## Controlled

Hold the state yourself with `pressed` and `onPressedChange`. Here it filters the list under it; the count is `tabular-nums`, so it never jitters as it changes.

```tsx
const [unreadOnly, setUnreadOnly] = useState(false)

<Toggle size="sm" pressed={unreadOnly} onPressedChange={setUnreadOnly}>
  <EnvelopeSimple weight="bold" /> Unread only
</Toggle>
```

## Disabled

`disabled` dims the control in either state and takes it out of the pointer's way, so a locked setting still shows which way it is set.

```tsx
<Toggle disabled><GridFour weight="bold" /> Show grid</Toggle>
<Toggle disabled defaultPressed><GridFour weight="bold" /> Show grid</Toggle>
```

## API reference

### Toggle

A `<button>` with `aria-pressed` and `data-state="on" | "off"`. Props: `variant` (`outline` · `ghost`), `size` (`sm` · `md`), `iconOnly`, plus Radix's `pressed`, `defaultPressed`, `onPressedChange`, `disabled` and every button prop. `className` is merged last.

### ToggleIcon

A decorative `<span>` that cross-fades two glyphs on the surrounding toggle's state. Props: `off` (the glyph at rest), `on` (the glyph while pressed), `className`. It reads the state through the toggle's `group/toggle` hook, so it only works inside a `Toggle`.

## FAQ

### Toggle, Toggle Group or Switch?

A Switch is a setting that applies on its own (notifications on). A Toggle is a button that stays pressed, usually beside other controls (bookmark, mute, unread only). A Toggle Group is a set of them, holding one choice or several.

### Why doesn't it shrink when I press it?

The pressed paint is the feedback. A control that shrinks on click and then changes its paint does two things for one gesture, so the Toggle only does the one that stays.

### Why are the heights 32 and 40, not the 36 of a Button?

They are Toggle Group's heights. A Toggle most often sits beside a group or stands in for a one-item group, and the two should line up. Inside a Toolbar, use the Toolbar's own toggle items, which follow the bar's scale.

### How do I name an icon-only toggle?

With `aria-label`, which also becomes what a screen reader announces with its pressed state ("Bookmark, toggle button, pressed"). Add a Tooltip carrying the same name for sighted users.

### Does the glyph cross-fade respect reduced motion?

Yes. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the two glyphs swap without the transition.

- Koala lib helpers it uses: `hit-area`, `tv`
